Subject: Horizon Health — working session logistics & room flow

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time to run this POC with us. To make the hands-on session productive I wanted to align on logistics early so we can avoid last-minute access or A/V surprises. Proposed approach:

- Format: hybrid but leaning onsite for the hands-on prompts/workbench.
- Duration: two half-days (Day 1: prompt review, routing, and security; Day 2: load and throughput tests + tuning).
- Redwood attendees: myself (Eng), Rishi (Sales Engineering), Vanessa (Customer Success).
- Asks for Horizon: confirmed room capacity, A/V for screen share + recording permission, visitor badge process and escort rules.

Proposed time windows (please confirm):
- Day 1: 09:30–13:00 (working session + 30m breakouts)
- Day 2: 13:00–17:00 (networking + load tests 15:00–16:00)

Attachments: initial_agenda.pdf (draft agenda).

If Horizon would prefer fully virtual, we can convert the same agenda to breakout rooms and remote routing tests, but the throughput/load validation will be easier with on-prem network access or a stable tunnel.

Next steps: can you confirm attendee list and whether Redwood is allowed to record the sessions for internal QA? Also: do you need us to provide an IP allowlist or will you provide a static endpoint?

Best,
Neha Kapoor

- Headcount: ~10 attendees from our Product/Integration teams (I attached attendee_names.xlsx).

Thanks Samantha — great questions. Quick answers and an updated plan below.

- Recording retention: Redwood is fine with recorded sessions for internal QA provided Horizon signs the short recording addendum; we can limit retention to 90 days. I’ll loop in Legal for the addendum.
- NDA/MSA: our standard mutual NDA is usually enough to get started; for any traffic that includes customer PHI we’ll need the POC addendum (we can send both).
- PoC/PO: not required to run the hands-on session; procurement can issue a PO if you want dedicated reserved capacity but it’s not required for the demo/load tests.
- Network: for reliable load testing we recommend either (a) a temporary static IP allowlist for our test endpoint or (b) a short-lived VPN/tunnel. Please let us know which your security team prefers.

Logistics we propose (for Horizon to confirm):
- Day 1 (onsite preferred): 09:30–13:00 — prompt walk-through, routing rules, and prompt-engineering best practices.
- Day 2 (onsite): 13:00–17:00 — 15:00–16:00 dedicated model load tests (we’ll simulate traffic patterns).
- Rooms: one main room for demos + two small breakouts for prompts review. We can bring our own laptops; we’ll need a room with a projector and HDMI/USB-C.

Attachments included: room_layout.png (suggested footprint), visitor_instructions.docx (checklist for badges & escort).

Action items:
- Please confirm final attendee list and whether security can provide an allowlist or approve a tunnel.
- If Horizon is okay, I’ll send calendar invites for the proposed slots and a DocuSign link for NDA.

Best,
Neha
Neha Kapoor — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical notes from the SE side: 

- Test plan: we will bring two model variants (small/fast + medium accuracy). For the load window we recommend starting with 50 concurrent chat requests and ramping to 300 over 20 minutes to observe latency curves.
- Allowlist: static IP allowlist preferred. If you cannot provide that, a short-lived tunnel is okay but we need to verify NAT stability ahead of time.
- Preflight: please share representative payloads (2–3 example prompts) 48 hours before the session so we can pre-warm KV caches.
- Tokens: I’ll provision a time-limited test token and bring a preflight script (we’ll run the 10-minute smoke test 24 hours before the workshop).
- GPU notes: our Dedicated cluster can sustain the proposed ramp if requests average <150 tokens; if you expect longer contexts we should cap concurrency.

Link to internal runbook: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/poc-preflight (for reference).

-Rishi
